ideas.title: The $0 Part D plan is gone for 2027: stand-alone drug plan premiums are on track to jump 50%, from $34 to $51 a month, for anyone who doesn't switch by Dec 7
ideas.angle: A usable number with a deadline. KFF says no stand-alone Part D plans will have a $0 premium in 2027, so the 4 million-plus people in one now will pay something unless they shop around. The plan with the lowest average premium nationally is Wellcare Value Script at $6.50. AARP Medicare Rx Preferred goes from $126 to $204.50. The deductible cap rises to $700. The take: compare plans before Dec 7, because staying put is what produces the 50% figure. This pairs with Tuesday's roundup item on the 4.3 million people losing their Advantage or Part D plan.
ideas.why_now: Open enrollment runs through Dec 7, and KFF published this today (Oct 30). The next Friday roundup still lands with about a month left to switch.
ideas.is_it_real: This is KFF's independent analysis of CMS 2027 plan data. The $51 average is a projection that assumes current enrollees stay in their plans and leaves out people getting the Low-Income Subsidy. It's an enrollment-weighted average, not anyone's actual bill. KFF puts the jump down mainly to the loss of $0-premium plans. The release doesn't say whether the scaled-back Part D premium stabilization demonstration played a part, so don't claim a cause beyond what KFF says. I checked the numbers against the KFF page today: $34→$51, 4M+ in zero-premium PDPs, Wellcare $6.50, AARP $204.50, $700 deductible cap, $643 average PDP deductible.

items.title: The Average Monthly Premium for Medicare Part D Stand-Alone Plans Is Projected to Increase by 50% From $34 to $51 in 2027 Unless Enrollees Switch to Lower-Cost Plans
items.summary: A new KFF analysis finds that the average monthly premium for Medicare Part D coverage in stand-alone prescription drug plans (PDPs) will increase to $51 in 2027, up 50% from $34 in 2026, if current enrollees don’t switch into lower-premium plans during open enrollment, which runs through December 7.

items.title: Medicare Part D Premiums and Cost Sharing in 2027
items.summary: Medicare Part D is a voluntary outpatient prescription drug benefit for people with Medicare provided through private plans, including stand-alone prescription drug plans and Medicare Advantage plans that offer drug coverage. This analysis provides an overview of Medicare Part D premiums and cost sharing in 2027 and key trends over time.
